task: Keep the persistent Eclipse JDT build daemon optional for Java compiler development builds.
observation: The JDT client hardcoded one Eclipse executable path and failed when it was absent, even though the repository supports a standalone javac build. This made the incremental daemon a prerequisite instead of an optional optimization.
impact: The client now supports an explicit MOSS_JDT_EXECUTABLE override and selects the standalone javac build when the daemon is unavailable. A focused in-process check covered the fallback selection; daemon startup and shutdown were not exercised.

resolution.summary: A missing JDT executable now selects the standalone compiler build; daemon lifecycle remains available when configured.

task: Make the optional JDT development daemon discoverable and controllable without weakening the standalone compiler path.
observation: The build helper still relied on a fixed Eclipse path and had no status/start command; a failed startup could leave a child process behind. Discovery now uses `MOSS_JDT_EXECUTABLE` or PATH, explicit start/status/stop actions are available, failed starts clean up the child, and normal builds fall back to javac.
impact: The JDT daemon remains optional and has a testable lifecycle surface. Five mocked tests cover discovery, status, stop, startup cleanup, and javac fallback; live Eclipse startup/stop behavior is still unknown.

resolution.summary: Portable executable discovery, explicit lifecycle controls, failed-start cleanup, and standalone javac fallback are covered by focused mocked tests; actual Eclipse lifecycle remains unverified.
